result.summary: Exposes `interfaces::Chain` over IPC by adding Cap'n Proto schemas and proxy wrappers, split into a stable `Chain` interface and an `UnstableChain` interface. The stable interface covers basic block lookups for external clients, while `UnstableChain` exposes the remaining methods for Bitcoin Core's own internal clients. It also updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree and makes minor adjustments to `interfaces::Chain` method signatures for proxy compatibility.
result.problem: Processes connecting to `bitcoin-node` over IPC cannot access chain data or subscribe to chain events, blocking out-of-process wallet separation (#10102). Exposing the entire internal `interfaces::Chain` interface directly to third parties would freeze internal wallet APIs against future refactoring.
evidence: PR description: "Processes connected to `bitcoin-node` over IPC (with `-ipcbind`) can use the `Mining` interface, but they can't currently use the `Chain` interface read chain data or follow chain events. Chain data could be useful to third-party clients and Bitcoin Core's own wallet could use this as well to run in a separate process (#10102)."
PR description citing #34981: "But exposing all of `interfaces::Chain` to external clients would make its methods hard to change, since the wallet uses them as internal API (#34981)."
result.scope_notes: Carries a large `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree update to version 14 along with substantial Cap'n Proto schema and proxy generation code.
result.changed_since_previous: The interface is now split into a stable Cap'n Proto `Chain` interface and an `UnstableChain` interface rather than exposing the whole interface identically; the libmultiprocess subtree update is refreshed to v14; and an explicit dependency on crash fix #36520 is noted.
result.card: Exposes the Chain interface over IPC using Cap'n Proto, splitting it into a version-stable Chain interface with basic block lookup methods and an UnstableChain interface for Bitcoin Core internal consumers. Currently, chain data and notifications are inaccessible over IPC, blocking multiprocess wallet separation (#10102) and external clients connecting via -ipcbind. This is a core prerequisite for running the wallet in an isolated process (#19460) and depends on #36520.

risk.why: Flaws in IPC serialization or input validation could allow connected IPC clients to crash or stall the node process.
